method: Concepts enumerated per BP-D31 step 1 from headings, defined terms, enumerated rules and named flags. Each concept carries the source line range and one or more probes; a probe is a regex that must match in at least one framework artifact for the concept to count as DEMONSTRATED. A concept with no probes is NOT DEMONSTRATED by construction. Probes target artifact identity (ontology IRIs, vocabulary terms, executable code) rather than file paths, after a v1.1.1 finding that a path-shaped probe can pass for reasons unrelated to the concept.

concepts.name: Blueprint layer (ontology-grounded domain model)
Product Backlog layer (machine-checkable register)
Product Roadmap layer (live computed view)
Layer separation: roadmap must not be a maintained document
Governance-domain classification of capability (how correctness is enforced)
Full life-cycle sweep per core entity
Check each stage against running code, not item titles
Business continuity/support is a first-class capability class
A blueprint gap is a defect, written down explicitly
TBox / ABox / Rules separation
concepts.note: Probes target the three distinct ontology IRIs, not filenames: the earlier filename probes passed only because the tooling pinned those paths, so removing the pins broke a probe that was never testing the concept.

concepts.name: PBI minimum fields: id, title, status
Every item scoreable OR explicitly flagged not-yet-scoreable with a reason
Done requires verifiable evidence (test id / version binding)
probes: L2: a Done item must carry at least one bridge-verified

concepts.name: Package is a deployable business capability, not a folder
isBusinessCapability=false groupings excluded from capability ranking
Dependency disclosed the moment it is stated in prose or judgement
Binary gap discipline: flagged vs silent gap, silent gaps driven to zero
WSJF throughput model with its components
Launch Readiness / MVP gate model (isLaunchGate, hasLaunchPriority)
Launch priority is owner-declared, never computed from WSJF
Package-level score is multi-factor judgement, never an average of child scores
100% member-complete is not itself risk-free or deployable
Rule R3 arbitration between the two prioritisation models, both answers printed
Roadmap is a script's output, computed every run
Retired document marked SUPERSEDED in place, not deleted
Report's eight required sections
Every report run is a verification, never a reused prior output
Version identity: versionInfo == versionIRI token == filename token (Gate K)
PATCH for fixes, MINOR for additions, priorVersion chain never squashed
concepts.note: Probes the chain itself (the priorVersion predicate plus both prior version IRIs) rather than one literal line, after a v1.2.0 finding that reformatting a multi-value predicate broke a single-line probe.

concepts.name: Four-gate release check: Gate 0, Gate P, Gate K, Gate R
A rule change documents the disagreement closed, the new logic, and the incident
Verify directly; never trust memory of a prior run
Flag undecided items explicitly; never guess a number
Every what's-next answer traceable to a run in the same turn
Owner role: launch-gate business calls, never computed
Builder role: multi-factor judgement with written rationale, maintains gates
